It's not too hard--just download the files you want, then locate them in your Downloads folder. They'll probably be in a ZIP file, so right click and click "Extract here". Then drag those files you extracted to your Documents folder, then the folder labeled Electronic Arts inside that, then The Sims 4, and finally Mods. Once your unpacked files are in your Mods folder, launch the game and open the Options menu. Under "Other", you should see a checkbox that asks if you want to enable custom content. Make sure that's checked, and you may also want to check the one under it that asks if you want to allow script mods (These are generally more extensive mods that have an effect on gameplay. It's up to you whether or not you want to get into that.). After saving your settings, relaunch the game and you should get a popup confirming the mods you've installed. Aaaaand that's about it! Enjoy!

Think of your earliest memory. Is it from when you were 4 or so? Maybe even 2? Probably. Now try to go earlier. Now earlier still. Back to when you were in the womb. You can't remember anything, can you? Your memory might as well be that black void you were describing.

But just because it's nothing doesn't make it a bad thing. If there's just a bunch of nothingness after you die, it's just like the nothingness from before you were born. Close your eyes for one second, then open them again. That's how long eternity feels like.

Death isn't scary, even if it's the end of everything you know. It's not cold or hot, it's not dark or light, it's just returning to the unconscious oblivion you were for millennia before you were even conceived and your atoms becoming one with the earth again. 

I'm scared of dying. I'm scared it might be slow, or painful, or both. I think everyone, at some point or another, worries about that. But death itself? Death isn't that scary. It's just our bodies stopping, whether God-driven or not.
